'''Saeki clan''' (佐伯氏) refers to a group of families bearing the name "Saeki" as their {{ill|Uji (clan)|en|Uji (clan)|qid=Q2575910|lt=Uji}} (clan name).
__TOC__{{-}}
== Overview ==
The Saeki clan traces its origins to {{ill|Ama-no-Oshihi|ja|天押日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenootsuhiko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシヒ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10939616|2=ja|3=アメノオシヒ|4=zh|5=天忍日命}} (Ame no Oshi-hi no Mikoto), who guided {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニニギ}} during the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|qid=Q1084733|lt=Descent of the heavenly grandson}}. The clan split from the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|en|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|qid=Q17227938|lt=Ōtomo clan}} under the leadership of {{ill|Ōtomo Muroya|ja|大伴室屋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtomo no Muroya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11432336}}, becoming a {{ill|Shinbetsu|ja|神別|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbetsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbetsu|qq=}} (descendant of deities) lineage of {{ill|Amatsukami and Kunitsukami|ja|天津神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11442793}} origin. The clan name "Saeki" is believed to derive from their role in guarding the imperial court, as they were seen as those who "block (遮 sahe) external threats." This evolved into "Saeki" (さえき) in modern phonetics, and in some cases as "Saiki" (さゐき).
The Saeki clan served as {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|ja|伴造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomonomiyatsuko|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, leading the {{ill|Saeki people|en|Saeki people|qid=Q7398288|lt=Saeki-be}}, who were tasked with guarding the {{ill|Royal court|en|Royal court|qid=Q1134237|lt=Imperial Court of Japan}}. The gates they protected were named "Saeki Gates," though during the Heian period, under {{ill|Tenpyō culture|ja|唐風文化|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang culture|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天平文化|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5525117}} influences, the name was changed to "Mokabe Gate" (藻壁門). Initially granted the {{ill|Kabane|ja|姓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabane|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of "Muraji" (連), the Saeki clan, alongside the Ōtomo clan and others, was elevated to the Rank of "Sukune" (宿禰) during the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign (685 CE).
Prominent figures in the Saeki clan included {{ill|Saeki no Komaro|ja|佐伯子麻呂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Komaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382809}}, who assisted in the assassination of Soga no Iruka, and {{ill|Saeki no Imaemishi|ja|佐伯今毛人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Imaemaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382787}}, a statesman who served as a {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|qid=Q1133663|lt=Sangi}} and {{ill|Dazai no Sochi|ja|太宰帥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dazai no Sochi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大宰帥}}. Military leaders such as {{ill|Saeki no Nifute|ja|佐伯丹経手|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Tsurugite|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q45828498}}, who served under Soga no Umako, and {{ill|Saeki no Iwayu|ja|佐伯石湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Ishiyu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382879}}, a general during campaigns against the Emishi, were also notable. However, by the end of the Heian period, the clan gradually declined from mid-level aristocracy to {{ill|Jigeke|ja|地下家|2=ja|3=地下家|lt=Jigeke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikage|13=User:Immanuelle/Jigeke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11424052}} (bureaucrats of lower Rank).
The Saeki name was carried on by families like the Ono family, who produced the herbalist {{ill|Ono Ranzan|en|Ono Ranzan|qid=Q11464264|lt=Ono Ranzan}}, and artists such as {{ill|Kishi Ganku|en|Kishi Ganku|qid=Q555061|lt=Kishi Ganku}} of the Kishi school.
== Related Lineages ==
=== Saeki no Miyatsuko (佐伯造) ===
The Saeki no Miyatsuko lineage is documented in the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}, appearing under the {{ill|Ukyo|en|Ukyo|qid=Q2474484|lt=Right Capital}} Shinbetsu. They were originally known as "Saeki-be" and managed the Saeki-be labor group.
=== Saeki no Obito (佐伯首) ===
The Saeki no Obito line appears in the Shinbetsu of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}} as recorded in the Shinsen Shōjiroku.
== Saeki-be ==
The Saeki-be, managed by the central Saeki clan, was a labor group organized as part of the {{ill|Shinabe clans|en|Shinabe clans|qid=Q11418456|lt=Shinbetsu}} system. Local Saeki-be groups were supervised by the {{ill|Nao Saeki|ja|佐伯直|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Ason|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382874}} lineage.
